bib.title: ZeRO-Offload: Democratizing Billion-Scale Model Training
bib.venue: USENIX ATC 2021 (text is arXiv v1 preprint, 18 Jan 2021)

read.skipped: Figure bodies (7-13) are images; only captions and surrounding text read. No appendix exists.

question: How can billion-scale transformer training fit on one or a few GPUs by offloading model states and optimizer compute to CPU without losing compute efficiency?
hypothesis: Offloading gradients, optimizer states and the optimizer step to CPU, while keeping fp16 parameters and forward/backward on GPU, is the unique strategy that minimizes CPU compute and CPU-GPU traffic while maximizing GPU memory savings.
contributions: A unique optimal offload strategy for GPU+CPU training enabling 10x larger models on a single GPU (Sec 3, 4.1)
Multi-GPU design combining offload with ZeRO-2 data parallelism and with model parallelism (Sec 4.2)
Fast SIMD CPU-Adam (over 6x vs PyTorch) and one-step delayed parameter update (Sec 5)
Evaluation: 13B on one GPU, 70B on a DGX-2, near-linear scaling to 128 GPUs

method.summary: Training is modelled as a weighted dataflow graph and partitioned between CPU and GPU. fp16 params and forward/backward stay on GPU; fp16 gradients, fp32 params/momentum/variance and the Adam update live on CPU. Combined with ZeRO-2 partitioning for multi-GPU, plus a SIMD CPU-Adam and an optional one-step delayed parameter update.

results.claim: ZeRO-Offload gives up to 1.33X/1.11X/1.64X the throughput of PyTorch/ZeRO-2/Megatron for 1B-15B models on 16 GPUs.
With 64 and 128 GPUs ZeRO-2 outperforms ZeRO-Offload, since batch sizes become similar and ZeRO-2 avoids CPU-GPU traffic.
L2L trains larger models than ZeRO-Offload on one GPU (17B) but does not scale with more GPUs.

limits: Strategy is derived only for mixed-precision Adam; other optimizers are not analysed.
Activation memory is not offloaded (footnote 1); relies on checkpointing.
On 64 and 128 GPUs ZeRO-2 is faster; offload mainly helps when GPUs are scarce.
CPU compute can bottleneck at small batch sizes; DPU changes training semantics and was verified only on GPT-2 (100K iterations) and BERT-large SQuAD, delayed 40 iterations.
No seeds or variance reported; GPT-2 data, learning rate and batch details not printed.
Single hardware platform (V100 32GB, PCIe, DGX-2); PCIe 32 GBps is the cost driver and has since changed (e.g. unified memory links).
Intro baseline 1.2B conflicts with 1.4B in Sec 6.2.1.
